your_book:
Monday's session delivered a split result for Jaleel's book. The biggest positive contributors were Boston Scientific (+4.82%), Adobe (+5.30%), and SAP (+5.78%) — the latter rallying on a somewhat counterintuitive catalyst: AI executives flagging that industry growth may need to slow, which traders read as reducing the competitive threat to incumbent enterprise software vendors. AutoZone (+3.09%) and AstraZeneca (+2.25%) also added solid ground. On the other side, NVIDIA fell 3.36% amid a cocktail of Middle East tensions, oil-driven inflation fears, and the same AI-slowdown signal that helped SAP — here interpreted as demand risk for chips — while Broadcom dropped 4.77% on directly related semiconductor pressure. Expand Energy slipped 1.51% on the oil-price read-through to inflation/rate concerns, and Rocket Lab edged down another 0.64%.

The drift problem is real and clustered. BSX is down 8.1% overall despite today's pop and carries an elevated risk flag — guidance was slashed to 7–8.5% growth and management guided flat through Q3, so the rally needs scrutiny rather than celebration. LULU sits at a −21.6% unrealized loss with a STRONG BUY verdict and an elevated guidance-cut flag; Americas comps are negative for the fifth straight period. RKLB is down 20.2% and rated AVOID — price and verdict are in the same direction, but position size at 6.5% is the issue. NVS is −14.6% with drug-pricing policy overhang. These are not paper cuts; they are thesis questions.

Watch NVDA into November 17 earnings — today's drop compounds export-control and AI-capex sentiment risk. Adobe's +5.3% day looks good on the surface, but the watch flag (AI-moat fear, CFO exit, narrative-not-numbers dynamic) hasn't cleared. The book remains in overall unrealized loss territory at −1.56%, and capital preservation demands that the divergence between STRONG BUY verdicts and multi-month negative returns gets re-examined, not rationalized.

attention.note: Rocket Lab carries the portfolio's largest single position among its worst-performing and only AVOID-rated holding; at a 6.5% weight in a capital-preservation book, the continued drag demands a size or exit decision, not monitoring.
